newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HOLDERS U.S. AND FAVOURITES SPAIN KNOCKED OUT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HOLDERS U.S. AND FAVOURITES SPAIN KNOCKED OUT.

text.p: Holders the United States and favourites Spain were bundled out of the Fed Cup on Sunday ending their recent domination of the women's team event.
The United States, under new coach Martina Navratilova, dropped both reverse singles to crash out 3-2 to the Netherlands, while Belgium won all four singles matches against Spain.
Spain have won four of the past six titles and defending champions the United States have won the competition 15 times since its inception in 1963.
They now face a play-off to stay in the top flight World Group One.
Brenda Schultz-McCarthy recovered from a nervous start to beat American Mary Joe Fernandez 1-6 6-4 9-7 and Miriam Oremans sealed the tie with a straight-sets win over Chanda Rubin in Haarlem.
The Netherlands will meet the Czech Republic, winners against Germany, in the semifinals in July.
Former world number one Arantxa Sanchez Vicario suffered her second defeat in two days to hand the Belgians an unexpected place in the semis where they will face France.
Sanchez Vicario, a shock loser to substitute Els Callens on Saturday, was beaten 6-3 2-6 8-6 by Sabine Appelmans in Sprimont, Belgium.
In the longest tie at the weekend, France survived two marathon rubbers and a surprise loss by Mary Pierce to beat Japan 4-1 in Tokyo.
After comfortably winning both singles on Saturday, Pierce and Nathalie Tauziat spent more than seven hours on court in two epic reverse singles matches.
Ai Sugiyama, world ranked 29, upset Australian Open finalist Pierce 7-5 6-7 6-4 in a contest lasting three hours and 10 minutes.
Tauziat's match lasted even longer. The French player needed four hours and five minutes to beat Naoko Sawamatsu 7-5 4-6 17-15.
